subject: ent
title: Sinusitis and its complications

steps.tx: Most colds with congestion reflect **acute viral rhinosinusitis** that improves within ten days, while **acute bacterial rhinosinusitis** declares itself through patterns: symptoms persisting beyond ten days without improvement, severe onset with fever, purulence and facial pain for three to four days, or **double worsening** after recovery. The **maxillary sinus** dominates adult disease, while ethmoid disease dominates children because frontal and sphenoid sinuses pneumatise later. Obstruction at the drainage channels, ciliary failure and allergy underlie episodes.
steps.say: Most sinus colds are viral and start improving within ten days. Bacterial infection is likely when symptoms persist beyond ten days without any improvement. Severe disease with high fever, thick discharge and facial pain also indicates bacterial infection. A cold that improves and then clearly worsens again needs review for bacterial sinusitis. Adult disease centres on the maxillary sinus while young children suffer ethmoid disease because frontal sinuses develop later.

steps.tx: Reserve **computed tomography** for complications, recurrent episodes, surgical planning or immunocompromise rather than routine colds. Examination and nasal endoscopy look for middle meatal pus, polyps or mucosal oedema. Reserve **amoxicillin** based treatment for cases meeting bacterial criteria, with analgesia, saline irrigation and **intranasal steroids** relieving symptoms. Unilateral maxillary disease with foul discharge suggests a dental root source from upper premolars or molars, and cure requires **dental source control** alongside sinus care.
steps.say: Scanning is reserved for complications and recurrent disease and for planning surgery, not for simple colds. Examination and endoscopy check the middle meatus for pus, polyps and swelling. Antibiotics are kept for cases that meet bacterial criteria while pain relief with saline washes and steroid sprays eases symptoms. Disease affecting one maxillary sinus with foul discharge should prompt inspection of the upper back teeth. Root infection remains until the dental source is treated.

steps.tx: Ethmoid sinusitis in children spreads easily through the thin **lamina papyracea** into the orbit, producing the Chandler sequence from preseptal cellulitis to **orbital cellulitis**, **subperiosteal abscess**, orbital abscess and **cavernous sinus thrombosis**. Proptosis, painful restriction of eye movements, chemosis, reduced vision or bilateral eye signs mark an emergency. Urgent contrast imaging with intravenous antibiotics and joint ENT and ophthalmology review decide the need for surgical drainage.
steps.say: Children with ethmoid sinusitis can develop orbital spread because the wall between the sinus and the orbit is very thin. Disease climbs from lid swelling to orbital cellulitis and abscess and finally to clotting in the cavernous sinus. A bulging eye with painful, restricted movements and reduced vision is an emergency. Bilateral eye signs suggest cavernous sinus involvement. Urgent contrast scanning with intravenous antibiotics and joint specialist review decides whether drainage is required.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating the escalating orbital complications of ethmoid sinusitis, from preseptal cellulitis to cavernous sinus thrombosis, highlighting the ethmoid sinus and lamina papyracea.
vis.caption: Orbital complications of ethmoid sinusitis (Chandler groups) progression

steps.tx: Frontal sinus infection can inflame the frontal bone and produce a tender forehead swelling called **Pott puffy tumour**, which risks epidural and subdural empyema. Further intracranial spread causes meningitis, **frontal lobe abscess** and **cavernous sinus thrombosis** with bilateral eye signs and sepsis. Sphenoid disease threatens the cavernous sinus, pituitary gland and carotid artery. Persistent chronic or complicated disease undergoes **functional endoscopic sinus surgery** to restore natural ventilation while protecting the orbit and skull base.
steps.say: A tender swelling on the forehead during frontal sinusitis means bone infection and needs urgent imaging. Infection can spread inside the skull and cause meningitis, collections of pus and brain abscess. Disease in the sphenoid sinus involves the cavernous sinus, the pituitary gland and the carotid artery. Bilateral eye signs with sepsis point toward cavernous sinus clotting. Chronic disease that resists medical treatment can undergo keyhole sinus surgery that restores natural drainage. The eye and the skull base need guarding throughout the operation.

steps.tx: The axial scan shows an opacified **frontal sinus** with soft tissue changes that carry **intracranial risk**. This matches the complication step where forehead swelling signals **Pott puffy tumour** with possible empyema beneath. In the exam, link frontal disease with urgent imaging, combined medical and surgical care, and referral before **cavernous sinus thrombosis** develops.
steps.say: This axial scan presents an opacified frontal sinus with changes that threaten the brain behind it. Forehead swelling with such a scan indicates bone infection that can seed pus inside the skull. Such cases require urgent imaging with combined medical and surgical care. Early referral prevents cavernous sinus clotting and brain abscess.
